description.value: This study examined structural and functional brain alterations in cocaine addiction using multimodal MRI, including brain tissue volume, baseline cerebral blood flow, and resting-state brain entropy, and evaluated multimodal classification of cocaine patients and controls.

spans.text: The purpose of this study was to examine both the structural and functional brain alterations in cocaine addiction regarding the above mentioned questions using multi-modal MRI including brain tissue volume, baseline CBF, and BEN.

value: cocaine-addicted brains would show both structural and functional alterations compared to controls, which are correlated with addiction-related behaviors
the multimodal brain alteration patterns in cocaine patients would show spatial overlap as well as discrepancies
combining multiple modalities (brain tissue, CBF, and the dynamic resting state property) will provide better brain discrimination sensitivity, as compared to single modality -based approaches

name.value: multi-modal imaging-based patient vs control brain classification

spans.text: To explicitly address this question, we calculated the voxel-wise inter-modality correlation and ran a multi-modal imaging-based patient vs control brain classification.

definition.value: patient vs control brain classification using combinations of tissue volume, CBF, and BEN data

spans.text: multi-modal imaging-based patient vs control brain classification
These ROI data were then used as multivariate features in a support-vector machine (SVM) learning-based patients vs control brain classification ( Wang et al., 2007a ; Zhang et al., 2014 ).
The imaging data of the testing subject was then input into the model to predict whether the subject was a patient or control.

Combining all three modalities yielded the highest classification accuracy than any other combination (84.6%), but tissue volume and CBF did not substantially add to the accuracy of BEN alone (79.5%).
39 leave-one-out cross-validations were used to verify the classification accuracy.

value: BEN provided the highest classification accuracy, while tissue volume provided the lowest.

Combining all three modalities yielded the highest classification accuracy than any other combination (84.6%), but tissue volume and CBF did not substantially add to the accuracy of BEN alone (79.5%).
Combining multi-modal imaging data can improve sensitivity for discriminating drug-addicted brain from non-drug dependent brain.

spans.text: For signal modality, BEN provided the highest classification accuracy, while tissue volume provided the lowest.
